t: Button with Longest Push Time — Single Scan
o: Each press's duration is the gap from the previous press; the first press's duration is its own timestamp. Return the index of the button with the largest duration, breaking ties by smallest index. In example 1 durations are 2, 3, 4, 6, so button 1 wins; in example 2 durations are 5 and 2, so button 10 wins. One linear scan suffices.
k: Durations are computable on the fly as time[i] - time[i-1]; track the best (duration, index) pair with strict-improvement rules to respect the tie-break.

a.n: Approach 1: Linear Scan Tracking the Best
a.i: Initialize the answer with the first event (duration = its time). For each subsequent event compute the gap; replace the best only when the gap is strictly larger, or equal with a strictly smaller button index — this exactly implements the tie-break.
s: Update best if dur > bestDur, or dur == bestDur and events[i].index < bestIndex.
a.t: O(n) — one pass over the events.

w: A one-pass argmax with a custom tie-break is all this needs. Pitfalls: forgetting that the FIRST event's duration is its raw timestamp (not zero), and using >= in the comparison, which breaks the smallest-index tie-break. Edge cases: a single event (return its index), repeated presses of the same button, and equal timestamps (duration 0). Follow-up: return all buttons achieving the maximum, or handle unsorted timestamps (sort first).
